requirements.quote:
An endpoint detects a potential Stateless Reset using the trailing 16
   bytes of the UDP datagram.
requirements.condition: When detecting a potential Stateless Reset from a UDP datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the trailing 16 bytes of the UDP datagram as the candidate stateless reset token.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can construct datagrams with controlled trailing bytes and verify that detection uses exactly the final 16 bytes.

requirements.required_behavior: Remember all associated stateless reset tokens.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be inspected after sending datagrams to verify retention of every associated token and its connection-ID and remote-address association.

requirements.condition: When maintaining the stateless reset tokens used to detect resets.
requirements.required_behavior: Include Stateless Reset Token field values received in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and the server's transport parameters.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply tokens through each named protocol source and verify that both become detection candidates.

requirements.condition: When maintaining stateless reset tokens used for detection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include tokens associated with unused or retired connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can mark connection IDs unused or retired and verify that their tokens are excluded from the detection set.

requirements.quote:
identifies a received datagram as a Stateless Reset by comparing the
   last 16 bytes of the datagram with all stateless reset tokens
   associated with the remote address on which the datagram was
   received.
requirements.condition: When determining whether a received datagram is a Stateless Reset.
requirements.required_behavior: Compare the datagram's last 16 bytes with all stateless reset tokens associated with the remote address on which it was received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use tokens associated only with other remote addresses as matches for the received datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can configure different token sets per remote address and verify the exact candidate set used for a received datagram.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MAY skip this check if any packet from a datagram is
   successfully processed.
requirements.condition: If any packet from an incoming datagram is successfully processed.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to skip the stateless reset token comparison.
requirements.why_checkable: Control-flow instrumentation can verify that skipping the comparison occurs only under the stated successful-processing condition.

requirements.quote:

   associated with a connection or cannot be decrypted.
requirements.condition: When the first packet in an incoming datagram cannot be associated with a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform the stateless reset token comparison.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Skip the stateless reset token comparison.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can provide an incoming datagram whose first packet has no connection association and observe whether comparison is performed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT check for any stateless reset tokens associated
   with connection IDs it has not used or for connection IDs that have
   been retired.
requirements.condition: When checking a received datagram for a Stateless Reset.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Check any stateless reset token associated with a connection ID the endpoint has not used.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can install a token for an unused connection ID and verify that a matching datagram is not checked against that token.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT check for any stateless reset tokens associated
   with connection IDs it has not used or for connection IDs that have
   been retired.
requirements.condition: When checking a received datagram for a Stateless Reset.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Check any stateless reset token associated with a retired connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can retire a connection ID and verify that its token is no longer used in stateless reset checks.

requirements.quote:
When comparing a datagram to stateless reset token values, endpoints
   MUST perform the comparison without leaking information about the
   value of the token.
requirements.condition: When comparing a datagram with stateless reset token values.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform the comparison without leaking information about token values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Expose token-value information through the comparison, including through token-dependent timing behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: The comparison implementation can be statically inspected and subjected to timing or side-channel tests to detect behavior dependent on token values.

requirements.quote:
If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a
   stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period
   and not send any further packets on this connection.
requirements.condition: If the datagram's last 16 bytes are identical in value to a stateless reset token.
requirements.why_checkable: A matching datagram can be injected and the endpoint's resulting connection state can be observed.

requirements.quote:
If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a
   stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period
   and not send any further packets on this connection.
requirements.condition: After the datagram's last 16 bytes match a stateless reset token.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send any further packets on the affected connection.
requirements.why_checkable: After injecting a matching datagram, outbound traffic can be monitored to verify that no further packet is sent on the connection.
